name: Gotland submarine HVDC link
description: A high-voltage direct-current submarine cable connected Gotland to mainland Sweden.

impact.note: One link serving one island; it improved the island's supply, and the commercial line of high-voltage direct-current transmission grew from this project.

places.note: Modern country or regional reference; historic political boundaries are not implied.

date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: A submarine high-voltage direct-current link between mainland Sweden and Gotland entered service. Its converters used mercury-arc valves.
events.caveats: Sources disagree about the month; earlier high-voltage direct-current transmission existed.

evidence.supports: IEEE account dates commissioning to 1954 and reports its rating.
Identifies the 1954 Gotland 1 installation and its mercury-arc valves.
IEEE account states ASEA commissioned the link.

date.basis: The supplier’s account dates the trial substitution to spring 1967.

events.statement: A thyristor valve was tried in place of one mercury-arc valve on the existing Gotland 1 link.
events.scope: Single valve trial on an operating link.

evidence.supports: Reports a spring 1967 trial of one replacement thyristor valve.

date.basis: The operator’s technical report dates the mixed-valve installation to 1970.

events.statement: Gotland 1 entered service in an upgraded configuration with thyristor valve groups added in series with its mercury-arc groups, raising the link’s capacity from 20 to 30 MW.
events.scope: Gotland 1 upgrade using both mercury-arc and thyristor valves.

evidence.supports: Dates the addition and confirms the mixed converter arrangement and increased capacity.
Independently describes both converter stations’ upgrade and service in spring 1970.

date.basis: The operator’s feasibility study dates removal of the original link to 1986.

events.statement: The original Gotland 1 cable and terminal equipment were taken out of service and dismantled.
events.scope: Original Gotland 1 cable and terminal equipment.

evidence.supports: Dates decommissioning and dismantling to 1986, during the construction of Gotland 3.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest event sourced for this particular record; not a claim of global origin.

caveats: The 1954 link is not presented as the first direct-current transmission experiment.

measures.subject: Gotland link
measures.conditions: IEEE account, initial link rating, not delivered energy.

measures.subject: Gotland submarine link
measures.conditions: IEEE table lists 96 km cable length.

research.note: Initial sourced admission; classification and interpretations await independent review. Independent reader checked 1954, 20 MW and 96 km against Tiku table 1 after source URL repair; month is conservatively omitted. The mercury-arc equipment, thyristor trial, hybrid upgrade and retirement are newly sourced proposals awaiting independent review.
